This passage is from **Homer's *Iliad*, Book 19, lines 184–197**. In this scene, Agamemnon is responding to Odysseus, agreeing to the terms for reconciliation with Achilles.

Here is the translation:

> Then the lord of men Agamemnon spoke to him again:
> "Son of Laertes, I rejoice to hear this word from you,
> for you have reached and recounted all things fittingly.
> I am willing to swear to these things, and my spirit urges me,
> nor will I swear falsely before the god. But let Achilles
> remain there, though eager for war, until
> the gifts come from the hut, and we cut the sacrificial oaths.
> And let all the others remain together.
> But to you yourself I enjoin and command this:
> choosing the young men, the best of all the Achaeans,
> bring the gifts from beside my ship, as many as to Achilles
> we promised yesterday to give, and bring the women.
> And let Talthybius quickly through the wide host of the Achaeans
> make ready a boar to sacrifice to Zeus and Helios."

***

**Notes on specific terms:**
*   **"Cut the sacrificial oaths" (ὅρκια πιστὰ τάμωμεν):** In Homeric ritual, oaths were sealed by sacrificing an animal and cutting its throat. The phrase literally means "cut the oaths."
*   **"Son of Laertes" (Λαερτιάδη):** A patronymic referring to Odysseus.
*   **"Talthybius" (Ταλθύβιος):** The herald of Agamemnon.
*   **"Helios" (Ἠελίῳ):** The personification of the Sun, invoked as a witness to oaths.
